items.text: Fugue of Tragedies

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Pride killed him in the end.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: His lies became the bullet that struck him down.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But it is all meaningless now.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Do you wish you'd stopped her?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... don't know.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Partita's set to be executed before the hospital pulls out today.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: No one in the company was willing to pull the trigger.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: So we drew straws. Franz pulled the short one.
A heavy silence falls. No one in this world will ever know Charon's expression in this moment.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: What happened with that photograph?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fabien has passed. He will be put to rest beside the others in the hospital that could not return home.
His commander and friend casts him a silent glance, unsure of what to say.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Upon return to the field hospital, he was already gone.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The photograph ultimately failed to find its way into his hands. He died never knowing that Anna awaited him at home.
Eberhard, finally overcoming his indecision, pulls a crumpled letter from his pocket and hands it to Charon.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Wilhelm gave me this letter. It came in from the rear this morning.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Their house—Fabien's and his wife's—burned down about a week ago.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... What? Why?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Bad news reaches the rear every day. Not everyone in the fatherland can bear the waiting.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fabien ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Vows were broken. He was alone when death came for him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Franz shielded a ghost from a bullet, but all that can be done is to apologize.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Partita chose her path. Ours is a deal that no longer has meaning.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Nothing of what is done here has any meaning at all.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: You're not sorry you didn't stop her?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Correct.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But "I" regret that Walter could not be saved.
Forest Near the Field Hospital
The soldiers escorting the withdrawal linger nearby, chatting and rolling cigarettes between their fingers.
Partita sits quietly off to the side, back straight, gaze unwavering.
As Charon approaches, the soldiers flanking Partita rise and give him a brief nod.
Charon offers them two packs of cigarettes. They politely decline and leave.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: The weather's nice today.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Not like the day you and Walter left, all rain and fog.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I could hardly make out your faces through the car window back then.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Have you found peace?
She smiles.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Peace?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Throw a handful of dirt into the abyss, and all you'll hear is the echo.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: That's all there is.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Enough about me, Paul.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: What about you? Will you keep burying the fallen?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes. This road knows no end. As long as war remains, so shall it continue.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Hah ... You never talked like that before you became a soldier.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: So, you came to the front to become a philosopher, did you?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: What happened, Paul? You haven't cracked a single joke since we ran into each other again.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You've turned dull.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Apologies ... Laughter's toll feels unbearably heavy now.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Even among the dead, there are those that cannot rest.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Well, at least you can still make fun of yourself—even if you do sound serious.
The soldiers begin to stir, their eyes drifting toward the two of them.
Partita notices and stares back at them.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You know I'm not some clueless little Fräulein, don't you?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: ... I've figured something out about you.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Something you haven't realized, or maybe refuse to acknowledge.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: It doesn't matter. Thank you, Charon.
His fingers twitch slightly.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I hope I'm not the last person to see the pain inside you.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I hope you one day find who you truly are.
"There is no 'me' left to find." That is what he wishes he could say, but the words fail to materialize.
She stands up and walks toward the soldiers.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Partita—
She doesn't look back.
Charon watches as Franz picks up his rifle. Noticing his stare, Franz turns away, as stiff and cold as stone.
Something stirs in the space where his innards should be and spreads through every inch of him.
Each throbbing wave of it racks Charon with unease, but all he can do is watch as Franz loads the bullet.
Franz's expression is blurred, distant, unfamiliar—as though he's hiding behind a soldier's mask to execute his duty.
And just like that—it's done.
Franz doesn't even glance at Charon. He simply slips into the line of soldiers and boards the transport.
The convoy roars to life, grinding over scorched ground and dying weeds.
Silence returns.
Only the dead remain, awaiting his hand to bury them beneath the earth.
Fabien, Partita, countless others—the young, tortured faces of war.
He walks alone to meet them, to carry out his last and only duty.
He raises the shovel and plunges it into the earth.
